detailed_description: The Time Calculator performs precise temporal arithmetic operations using ISO 8601-compliant date-time parsing and JavaScript's ECMAScript Internationalization API for accurate timezone handling. This tool enables users to execute three core operations: addition of durations to timestamps, subtraction of time intervals, and bidirectional difference calculation between two datetime values. Built with DST-aware logic, it automatically adjusts for daylight saving time transitions using IANA Time Zone Database mappings. The engine converts input strings to epoch timestamps for calculation, preserving nanosecond precision through WebAssembly-based arithmetic handlers. Users benefit from its ability to handle complex scenarios like cross-timezone duration calculations, server log analysis with millisecond precision, and financial instrument expiry computations requiring ISO week date conversions. The tool's unique temporal diff algorithm outputs results in configurable formats including HH:MM:SS, total seconds, or mixed units with fractional precision.
usage_steps: Select calculation mode using the operation dropdown (Add Time, Subtract Time, or Calculate Difference)
Enter primary timestamp in the 'Start Time' field using ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) or Unix epoch
Input time interval in the duration field using format P[n]Y[n]M[n]DT[n]H[n]M[n]S (ISO 8601 duration syntax)
Choose timezone context from the dropdown (UTC, Local, or specific zone like America/New_York)
Click 'Calculate' to execute operation with leap second compensation
Review results displayed in both raw epoch format and human-readable localized datetime
usage_examples: Calculating AWS Lambda execution duration across daylight saving boundary by inputting start/end timestamps
Determining meeting window feasibility between Tokyo and London teams considering current timezone offsets
Validating PCI DSS certificate expiration intervals with precise 3-year increments including leap years
Analyzing server response times by subtracting nanosecond-resolution timestamps from application logs
